ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
What is the reason that the lightest member of Group 15 does not follow the trend of the other members, which show that the boiling point decreases with decreasing atomic mass of the Group 15 element?
The graph shows the variation of boiling point with Group number for the hydrogen compounds of the four lightest members of Group 15 on the periodic table (NH3, PH3, AsH3 and SbH3).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a line graph of the boiling point changes of Group 15 hydrides; the vertical-axis boiling point goes from about 0 to -100. PH3, AsH3, and SbH3 roughly show the trend that the boiling point increases as the mass of the central atom increases, while NH3, as the lightest Group 15 hydride, does not have its boiling point drop lower according to this trend, but instead is abnormally high. Reasoning: The question asks about the type of intermolecular force that causes NH3 to deviate from the boiling point trend of PH3, AsH3, and SbH3. NH3 contains N-H bonds, the nitrogen atom has strong electronegativity and has a lone pair of electrons, and hydrogen bonds can form between molecules; hydrogen bonding strengthens intermolecular attraction and raises the boiling point. Therefore the answer is hydrogen bonding.
